0.desc: Well-focused, consistently stained, densely cellular epithelioid/polygonal tumour-like fields with moderate cytoplasm and readily discernible nuclei.

1.candidate_biological_interpretation: Predominantly compact viable tumour-like tissue with tumour-host/interface admixture.
1.desc: More basophilic compact tumour-like fields than C0, with higher nuclear-to-cytoplasmic appearance and recurrent admixture of tissue edge, fibrous, vascular, muscle-like or fascicle-like host structures.

2.candidate_biological_interpretation: Low-contrast viable-tumour-like tissue is possible, but focus/stain/scan quality remains an equally plausible driver.
2.desc: Soft-focus, lower-contrast cellular-appearing fields with variable discohesion, clefting and partial tissue loss; fine nuclear detail is unreliable and slide-specific technical effects remain a major concern.

3.candidate_biological_interpretation: Necrosis-enriched injury-like tumour tissue with focal haemorrhage and residual viable, inflammatory or stromal components; a candidate treatment-emergent response phenotype.
3.desc: Predominantly pale eosinophilic tissue with ghost-cell-like outlines, fading or loss of nuclei, scattered pyknotic/karyorrhectic debris and architectural disintegration; a minority of exemplars are more cellular, stromal or haemorrhagic.
3.morphology_interpretation: Residual detected nuclei are descriptive only: necrotic-core nuclei may be lysed, fragmented or misclassified, so within-C3 nuclear morphology requires explicit segmentation QC and is not a viable-tumour treatment contrast.
3.treatment_interpretation: The observed presence in both PLX mice and absence in both Vehicle mice is a treatment-associated architecture signal; causal drug-induced necrosis or efficacy is not established.

4.candidate_biological_interpretation: Background/section boundary with sparse host connective, vascular or debris-like material rather than a coherent tumour state.
4.desc: Predominantly white background, thin section-edge fragments, loose pale connective tissue, isolated vessels or erythrocytes, debris and occasional degenerate tissue; tissue content is inconsistent and often minimal.

centralQuestion.question: Do neoplastic cells in control and PLX-treated tumours have different morphologies?
centralQuestion.roleOfThisStage: Establish whether neoplastic-cell morphology differs between frozen tissue contexts, before interpreting within-context treatment comparisons.
centralQuestion.plainLanguageAnswer: The image-defined tissue contexts have distinguishable but overlapping nuclear profiles. Whether those differences generalise across held-out mice is quantified by the tile-level classifiers.

analysisContract.primaryHierarchy: nucleus -> tile median -> equal tiles within mouse -> equal mice
analysisContract.allNucleiPooledView: descriptive only; never used for treatment inference
analysisContract.classifierValidation: leave one mouse/WSI out; preprocessing fit on training mice only
analysisContract.clusterIdentityScope: run-local; C# values are not aligned across cohorts

interpretationRules: Good morphology-only performance across held-out mice supports cross-slide concordance between nuclear shape and tissue context.
A material gain after adding composition suggests clusters are distinguished partly by cellular mixture or density.
Poor held-out-mouse performance despite within-section separation is compatible with slide, stain, or segmentation specificity.
Classification accuracy is not independent pathology validation and makes no treatment-effect claim.

limitations: Only 4 mice are available, with one WSI per mouse.
Clusters outside the provenance-resolved morphology-evaluable role gate have neoplastic morphology shown as N/A, not zero.
Cluster labels and nuclear measurements originate from the same H&E sections; classification is internal concordance, not independent validation.
No anatomical identity, lymph-node identity, necrosis, or drug-affected label is assigned without pathologist review.
The all-nuclei pooled view overweights large slides and nucleus-rich tiles and is descriptive only.
Area and perimeter, and several outline features, are correlated; they are complementary views rather than independent confirmations.
